subject: Deployment qualification & security sync — Acadia Health Systems
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Simmons <r.simmons@acadiahealth.com>, Tom Barrett <tom.barrett@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment qualification & next steps (BAA/SOC2/KMS)

Hi Rachel / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of options we walked through (tradeoffs for Acadia):
- Hosted API (Redwood-managed): fastest to production, broadest feature set, requires BAA for PHI and SOC2 evidence; shorter onboarding (days/weeks).
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput + tenant isolation; good middle ground if you want more control without full private ops.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): for regulated PHI workloads where you must own network boundary and keys — longer lead time (weeks-months) and procurement/infra coordination.

Compliance and technical asks we noted:
1) Data classification: please confirm whether the production dataset will include PHI (you indicated yes).
2) BAA: we can share a draft — attaching a template for Acadia legal to review.
3) SOC 2 Type II: attached is a redacted SOC2 summary we can provide now; procurement/security may request full report under NDA.
4) Key management: confirm whether you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and region residency requirements.
5) Audit artifacts: event/audit logs, retention policy, and access review cadence — tell us which artifacts are required for your auditors.

Asks / next steps:
- Rachel/Tom: please confirm data classification (PHI yes/no) and whether procurement wants a draft BAA routed to legal.
- If PHI: indicate preference for Dedicated vs Private (we can recommend a migration path: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private).
- Please share any SOC2 control numbers or specific evidence requirements your auditors will enforce (e.g., CC6.1 encryption, CC7.4 key rotation).
- Security deep-dive: propose a 60-min sync Wed 4 Nov or Thu 5 Nov (9am PT or 11am PT). Which works?

Attachments: [Attachment: BAA-draft-Acadia.docx (docx, 120KB)], [Attachment: tokenized-soc2-redacted.pdf (pdf, 850KB)].

I'll loop Ben for pricing and Marissa for procurement coordination. If you want a quick pricing delta for Dedicated vs Private baseline, we can attach a short estimate.

Thanks — looking forward to the next sync.

—

Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment qualification & next steps (BAA/SOC2/KMS)

Thanks Soojin — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: the system will process PHI in production (patient notes + limited identifiers). We need BAA in place before we route prod traffic.
- SOC2: procurement/security will need evidence of SOC2 Type II; happy to receive the redacted summary. For the full report, our legal team requires it be shared under NDA.
- Keys: we prefer customer-managed KMS in our AWS account (customer key ownership). Is that supported for both Dedicated and Private? If not, please call out the options and tradeoffs.
- Timeline: if we go Private (VPC), what is the typical lead time and what infra commitments are needed from us? We want a ballpark (weeks).

Procurement has been copied — they will review the BAA draft. Can Ben/Marissa provide a short delta estimate (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) to include in our procurement packet?

Also, can you confirm data residency defaults for Hosted and Dedicated (are hosted endpoints US-only or multi-region)?

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Simmons

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment qualification & next steps (BAA/SOC2/KMS)

Looping in pricing/procurement details. Quick answers and recommended path:
- KMS: customer-managed keys in the customer's AWS account are supported for Dedicated and Private VPC deployments. For Hosted API we offer customer-managed KMS *options* for encrypting persistent storage but network and runtime remain Redwood-managed; we'll document control boundaries for legal.
- Lead time: Dedicated (reserved) can be provisioned in ~2–4 weeks depending on capacity; Private VPC typically ~4–8 weeks depending on network & onboarding (peering, IAM, customer infra review). On-prem has additional ops time.
- Recommended initial path for PHI: start on Dedicated (predictable performance + isolation) and plan a Private cutover if Acadia must own network boundaries or run entirely inside your VPC. This minimizes risk and procurement friction.

I'm attaching a concise estimate matrix (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with order-of-magnitude monthly run rates and typical onboarding effort. 

Ownership for next steps:
- Soojin: run technical/security deep-dive and capture required SOC2 controls/evidence list.
- Marissa: lead procurement packet and sizing/pricing for the Dedicated baseline.
- Ben: produce delta estimate and SLA language for the packet.

Propose security sync: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 at 09:00 PT. Will that work for Acadia?

[Attachment: deployment-estimate-matrix.csv (csv, 18KB)]
